extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of Canadian history, particularly those interested in the Royal Northwest Mounted Police and northern patrols
extracted.subtask_description: Chaptered historical narrative describing incidents, organizational practices, and the character and operations of the Royal Northwest Mounted Police in the early 20th century; includes implicit and explicit standards for patrol conduct, recruitment, training, and recognition of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired personal qualities of members
rubrics_metrics.description: “We require sober, trustworthy men; those who are not, only remain in the Force until they are found out.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond sobriety and trustworthiness, the text emphasizes superior individual quality: ability to act separately, individual initiative, reliability in judgment under sudden and unexpected conditions, physical endurance, and a love of adventure and duty. Examples/assessment notes: men who could be trusted 'even in detachments of one' were prized; the corps valued moral character and steadiness over pay incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing levels and detachment sizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner Perry stressed the need for increasing numbers of the Force because burdens were laid upon one man that should have been borne by two or three.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational standard: avoid chronically understaffed detachments. Consequences of under-staffing include doubled hours in the saddle, reduced recuperation, risk of breakdown. Policy guidance: expand manpower in line with geographic spread to prevent overwork despite individuals' high efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training policy and readiness at headquarters
rubrics_metrics.description: Perry's policy to have 'a goodly number of men always in training at headquarters so that unready recruits should not have to go out to face emergencies.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational guideline: maintain a training reserve to ensure field detachments are not filled with untrained men. Rationale: preserves operational reliability and avoids sending unready recruits into hazardous duties. Described as 'statesman-like' policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment motives and selection fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Men were attracted not by pay but by 'the love of the adventurous and the desire to do work in the out-of-the-way places.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruiting standard: select individuals who are suited by temperament for remote and hazardous service (adventure-seeking, sense of duty). Anti-pattern: relying on monetary incentives to fill posts needing particular character and resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patrol provisioning and equipment sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Patrols must carry sufficient provisions and equipment for men and dogs; under-provisioning and over-confidence in minimal supplies contributed to the Fitzgerald patrol disaster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance and lessons: carry ample food for both men and dogs, ensure warm sleeping-bags, adequate maps/compass, and contingency supplies; avoid 'not burdening' trains with too little food. Example/anti-pattern: the Fitzgerald party carried limited rations (10 lbs flour, 8 lbs bacon) and suffered fatal consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and retention of local guides
rubrics_metrics.description: The account criticizes the discharge of the hired Indian guide (Esau) before the party reached Dawson and notes the Commissioner's telegram asking why the Indian was discharged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational standard: retain competent local guides when traversing unfamiliar or maze-like river/mountain country. Anti-pattern: dismissing guides prematurely to save expense or because of overconfidence in a companion's memory of route; consequence can be becoming lost and catastrophic outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search party outfitting and mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Superintendent Snyder's orders to Corporal Dempster: 'Send a well-outfitted party.' and 'bearing in mind that nothing is to stand in your way until you have got into touch with this party.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for search operations: select experienced personnel familiar with country, outfit them thoroughly, give broad discretionary authority to be guided by circumstances and judgment, and prioritize contact with missing parties above other considerations. Example: Dempster's party succeeded because of experience and proper outfitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patrol perseverance ethic
rubrics_metrics.description: It was 'not the Police way to turn back when they were out on a definite errand.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural norm and evaluative dimension: perseverance and duty-based persistence are highly valued, even in extreme hardship. Cautionary note: this ethic, while admirable, can contribute to tragic outcomes (e.g., failure to turn back when route became uncertain contributed to deaths).

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer responsibility for men's environment and morale
rubrics_metrics.description: Superintendent Starnes sought modest comforts for men at remote posts: chairs instead of long benches, pictures, white crockery, a small billiard table, and additional books and magazines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management standard: provide reasonable comforts to improve morale at isolated posts within budgetary/censor constraints. Practical examples: small furnishings, crockery, recreational facilities and reading material help sustain men at dreary, forbidding stations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and ceremonial honors for fallen members
rubrics_metrics.description: The Force provided formal funeral rites, firing parties, memorial tablets, and renamings (e.g., Smith's Landing changed to Fitzgerald) to honor those who died in service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional standard for honoring service: perform all last rites possible under circumstances, arrange religious services where possible, provide military honors (firing party), raise funds for memorials, and record public commemoration to reflect the Force's esteem. Example: the Fitzgerald patrol received Christian burial rites, firing party, memorial tablet and place-name tribute.
